key_insight: Entrance-generated streamwise vortices in lab-scale DCMD cause Reynolds-number-dependent temperature polarization bias, shifting from stronger to weaker TP relative to a straight-channel baseline as flow rate increases.
engineering_relevance: Membrane-distillation correlations and module characterization should account for geometry- and Reynolds-dependent entrance effects, rather than using a single universal correction.
method: 3D CFD simulations of direct contact membrane distillation
Swept inlet Reynolds number from 10 to 1000
Varied side-chamber length and main-channel height to isolate geometry effects
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation-based evaluation across multiple geometries and flow conditions, showing vortex persistence and TP deviations that change systematically with Reynolds number.
watch_item: These findings are specific to the modeled lab-scale geometry and operating range, so direct transfer of any correction to other modules or higher-Re flows should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Reynolds-number-dependent entrance bias in temperature polarization of lab-scale membrane distillation
